page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 10.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.62 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the c5n.xlarge in the lower performance tiers for most compute and memory tasks. In stress-ng and Geekbench tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads, also rank in the bottom 25%, with Passmark memory scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench text processing, and text generation for small 135M parameter language models.

Given its dedicated compute allocation and network optimization, the c5n.xlarge offers a structured entry point for network-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external EBS volumes, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, network-intensive utility tasks, and moderate computational workloads that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon cores without demanding high memory throughput.
